title: Gen-CJ
fill_note: DENSE layered wind with a jig; scorer cap 0.65
fill_how: The scored turns assume a dense, layer-by-layer wind at fill 0.65 (insulated-wire area / window; the scorer cap). Use a winding jig on a drill/lathe with a turn counter, lay each layer side-by-side with light back-tension, and do not scramble-wind: a scramble wind only reaches ≈0.55–0.60 and then the window holds fewer turns (scorer what-if `--fill 0.60` is in the table above). Never wind more than the listed turns — the copper must stay below the flanges.
steel_extra: **New steel:** Ø198 discs, M3 clamp map R30 at 0/90/180/270° and R44 on the inter-pole angles 67.5/112.5/247.5/292.5° (both inside the R86 magnet ring). Cut from this kit's `steel_backiron_disc.dxf`; no earlier disc fits.
o5_note: 48 DIAMETRIC Ø5×5 fitted, 3 per inter-pole gap (R79.8/86/92.2), Halbach-oriented (rule engraved on every arc)
card_title: Gen-CJ · dual-rotor 8p/12c · RADIAL-block poles (Ø20 N52 + N42 20×10×5 radial) + Ø5 Halbach
card_sub: poles = Ø20 disc @R86 + N42 block @R64.5 (20 mm RADIAL) · 48 diametric Ø5 · bobbins r50–104 × 4.5 mm · 2× Ø198 steel · 2026-10-17
idea: Gen-CG refined: each N42 20×10×5 block is turned so its 20 mm side runs RADIALLY (centre R64.5, r54.5–74.5) right inside the Ø20 N52 disc at R86, giving a long, narrow 42 mm radial pole (r54.5–96). The narrow block leaves wide inter-pole gaps at the inner radius (less pole-to-pole leakage) and lets the bobbins reach in to r50, so each turn links more pole for the same 390 m spool. 48 diametric Ø5 Halbach columns in the gaps; same Ø229 annular stator OD, same Ø198 steel / clamp map as Gen-CG, one plate.
halb_block:
halbach_magnetisation = "diametric"; // O5x5 assist magnets MUST be DIAMETRICALLY magnetised (tangential)
rotor_b_same_axis   = true;     // same-index magnets share one axis: N faces S across the gap
